description: Find the provisions that refer to a given one — in the same law, in other laws, and in the Cabinet and Ministerial Orders (政令, 省令) that set the details it leaves to them: every provision in the laws japanlaw.org holds that cites the given one. Each with its law, designation, the words it cites with, an id for fetch and its url; link each one you name by its fromUrl. Call it with law and address, as get_provision: {"law": "labor-standards-act", "address": "Article 36(1)"}.

address.description: The provision, as the statute writes it (第三十六条第二項第一号), as the Ministry's English does (Article 36(2)(i)), or as japanlaw.org does (art-36/par-2/item-1). A bare number is an article: 36; the short forms people write read too: 36条2項, 3条の2, 39(5). Supplementary provisions use the site's addresses, which search and get_law hand out; an appended table is appdx-1 or 別表第一.

lang.description: The language of the pages every url opens, and of the card get_provision is drawn as: "en" (default) or "ja". The text returned always holds both languages.

law.description: The law: its Japanese title (労働基準法), English title (Labor Standards Act), short name (労基法), slug (labor-standards-act) or e-Gov law ID (322AC0000000049). A slug or English title a letter or two off is read as the one held law it is near, and note says so.

limit.description: How many to return, 1–300; default 50. total counts them all.

name: get_citing_provisions

note.description: What to know about this answer. Where the law was not named exactly, it opens by saying how it was read: a slug or English title a letter or two off read as the one held law it is near — "read 'labor-contract-act' as labor-contracts-act (労働契約法, Labor Contracts Act)".

title: Find what cites a provision
